title: Congress, AAP, Left protest alleged voter roll irregularities at Delhi CEO's office
seoTitle: Delhi protest against voter roll irregularities

tea.why: Protesters allege irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and widespread "vote theft" in Delhi.
tea.want: They demand to highlight failures in enrolling voters, especially minorities and the poor, and raise concerns about deleted voters.
tea.changed: Oct 7: AAP leaders and workers were stopped by police barricades while marching towards the Delhi CEO's office.

summary: On October 7, 2026, the Congress, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), and Left parties planned a protest march to the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer’s office at Kashmere Gate. The demonstration aimed to highlight alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, including the deletion of over 47 lakh voter names and notices issued to 33 lakh others, which an AAP leader described as "outright fraud." The Delhi Traffic Police issued an advisory, warning of traffic disruptions in the area. During the march, AAP leaders and workers were stopped by police personnel at barricades.
demands: Highlight failures of the Delhi CEO in enrolling voters
Raise concerns over more than 47 lakh people left out of the draft electoral roll
Raise concerns over 33 lakh voters served notices by the ECI
Challenge alleged "vote theft" and systematic voter deletions
Demand greater transparency in the Special Intensive Revision process
response: Police personnel stopped Aam Aadmi Party leaders and workers at barricades as they marched towards the Delhi CEO's office, according to ANI. The Delhi Traffic Police issued an advisory regarding traffic restrictions due to the proposed protest, according to The Hindu.

updates.text: Congress, AAP, and Left parties announced a protest march for the following day to the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office, according to party sources.
The Delhi Traffic Police issued an advisory, warning of traffic disruptions around Kashmere Gate due to the planned protest.
Aam Aadmi Party leaders and workers were stopped by police barricades while marching towards the Delhi CEO's office, alleging "vote theft."
